paragraphs: The S63 AMG has been the performance flagship of the S-Class range since 2008, spanning three generations. Early and mid-generation cars (W221 and W222, roughly 2008 to 2020) use the M157 — a 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 shared with several AMG models of that era. From 2020, the W223-generation S63 AMG switched to the M177, a newer 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear patterns differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every S63 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 fitted to the S63 AMG from 2008 to 2020, across two generations. Known for valve seal and coolant system wear over time — see the callout above. We replace these as standard on every M157 rebuild.

The current 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, fitted from 2020. A genuinely different design from the M157, with its own valve seal and coolant wear patterns consistent with the AMG V8 family. We replace these as standard on every M177 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the S63 AMG spans two distinct engines across three generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M157 part will work on an M177 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic S-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
